title: Locker and Recipe
premise: Ines Lockridge has spent three years perfecting invisibility: raise her siblings, keep grades up, never let anyone past the shut locker door. But when her history teacher pairs her with Theo Vance—her sharpest critic and the mayor's son—for a semester project on the town's founding, they uncover a forgotten recipe book that reveals Maple Hollow's centennial festival was built on Ines's great-great-grandmother's kitchen. When the town council votes to cancel the fading festival, Ines and Theo must recreate the lost recipes from a water-damaged manuscript, dragging Ines's family secrets into the light. The story ends at the revived centennial feast, where Ines finally opens her locker—and her life—to the town that remembers her name.
about_author: Mara Delacroix grew up in a small mill town where every family guarded one recipe like a birthright, and she still can't make pie crust without crying a little. She writes stories about loud families, quiet kids, and the kitchens where both learn to speak.

chapters.title: The Combination
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A morning routine montage: waking the twins, packing lunches, memorizing flashcards between bells. Her locker is her fortress—organized, anonymous, locked. The emotional beat is weary competence; Ines believes invisibility is safety, and we see exactly what it costs her.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Mr. Okafor announces semester pairs for the local history project: Lockridge and Vance. Theo sneers that she'll coast on 'tragedy points'; she fires back with his father's failed development deal. Forced to meet after school, they discover their only common ground is mutual contempt—and a shared deadline.

chapters.title: What the Archive Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Researching in the library basement, they find an 1890s community cookbook credited to Odile Lockridge—Ines's ancestor—with recipes labeled by family name. Theo realizes the centennial festival was literally built on her family's kitchen. The beat: reluctant awe, the first crack in the rivalry.

chapters.title: Water Damage
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Half the manuscript pages are ruined, including the festival's centerpiece recipe. At home, Mom works a double; Ines burns dinner trying to improvise from memory. Her little sister asks why they never talk about Great-Great-Grandma Odile. The beat: grief surfacing through ordinary failure.

chapters.title: The Council Agenda
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo learns his father plans to vote to cancel the money-losing festival and sell the square to developers—the same deal Theo once defended. Guilt and ambition collide. He shows Ines the agenda item without telling her about his father's role. Beat: complicity and the fear of choosing sides.

chapters.title: Test Kitchen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pair starts recreating damaged recipes by trial and error in Ines's cramped kitchen, siblings drafted as taste-testers. Failures become jokes; Theo sees the weight Ines carries, and she sees past his polish. Beat: warmth arriving uninvited, and Ines hating how much she doesn't hate it.

chapters.title: Rumors and Ruin
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A classmate photographs Ines and Theo together; gossip twists it, and Theo goes cold in public to protect his reputation. Worse, the recipe pages go missing from the archive. Ines suspects sabotage but can't prove it. Beat: betrayal, old armor going back on.

chapters.title: Odile's Margins
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds the missing pages hidden inside a framed photo in his own house—his grandfather took them decades ago as leverage against the Lockridge land claim. Confronting his father means ending the version of himself he's performed all his life. Beat: the choice between inheritance and integrity.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the council meeting, Theo publicly returns the pages and testifies against the sale; Ines reads Odile's margin notes aloud—recipes written for neighbors who couldn't afford their own flour. The room turns. The festival is saved by one vote. Beat: climax, courage made public.

chapters.title: Centennial
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Graduation week: the town cooks Odile's menu together on the square, Ines's siblings running the dessert table, Mom off shift and present for once. Theo stands beside her, not behind or across. She spins her locker combination open one last time and leaves it empty. Beat: belonging, chosen and earned.
